candidates.review_text:
I came here on a Friday night for dinner. The atmosphere is very homey feeling and it feels as if you're sitting in someone's apartment eating. It is pretty tight quarters inside. We sat just inside the door in the first room, so I am not sure if other rooms/seating areas are bigger. 

I ordered the Greek sausage dish and my girlfriend ordered the veggie stuffed peppers. Overall the meal was good. It was nothing extravagant or special however. It did taste homemade which was nice and authentic. Both of our meals came with a lot of rice, which is good, but for the price I would have liked a little more substance. The Greek sausage dish consists of sliced sausages in a marinara sauce with sautéed peppers over rice. It was tasty, but for $19 is a bit overpriced in my opinion. 

Overall the meals were good, but nothing special. It is very Greek and tasted authentic which was nice. The meals were a bit overpriced for what they consisted of.
Great food and wonderful experience! The only issue would be the price compared to portion size-- for the appetizers. The entree portions are generous and worth the price!

My hubby ate here for the first time a few weeks ago and couldn't stop talking about it, so naturally he forced me to eat there. We ordered a feast like, 30 minutes before closing time, but the service was still top-notch and the food came out fast. 

The food was affordable, and came with a lot!! The average price of a meal is around $8 or $9, with affordable priced sides and desserts.  For the value, the food was fantastic and I recommend that if you are in the area you try this place out!

Not bad. Expensive but not bad. Does seem a little overpriced though for what is worth. Good definitely but I would expect a larger size of food for the price we were paying. Not Rly enough in that area. Good food overall though.
So we did take out and were very pleasantly surprised. The food was delicious, the portions good, and reasonably priced! Our expectations were definitely exceeded!

The service is very good. Restaurant is beautiful, and feels elegant. I thought overall, the food and portions were decent. Enjoyed the drunken noodles and mixed veggies we got. Prices were steep ($14-$30 for most entrees). Overall, it was a good experience considering how spot on the service was, but expensive for what you get.

Visiting Philly and got the recommendation to come here from some locals. It was phenomenal!! First thing you notice is the cozy yet hip decor and then you find the wine list which is quite extensive and quite impressive with a large variety of price points. A huge selection of wines by the glass and bottles alike. Ordered a variety of tapas to share for the three of us with some notables including the calamari, cheese board with some of the best bleu cheese I've ever had, octopus, peppers and some others. Waitress and overall service was phenomenal with quick turnaround times on the food and my water glass was never empty.  The wine manager even stopped by to say hello which was a nice touch. The staff here definitely seemed enthusiastic about their menu/wine list. A MUST TRY if you are in the area. Did I mention the meal was extremely affordable as well, seriously there are no excuses to not try this place out!

Half an hour wait at 11:30 on a Sunday.  (Unfortunately my punctual friend had to endure this as Septa got me there around 25 minutes late!)  An interesting industrial feel.  You walk in the door and immediately up a set of stairs to a concrete room with big pipes and big wheel valves you're not supposed to touch.  The room is warm though, covered in local art.  Service was pleasant.  The meals around the room looked ample and made us salivate.  The menu and specials both looked fantastic.  I tried the special "baked egg."  ("Diced potatoes, white beans, sweet onions,  Long hot peppers and shredded pork simmered in a spicy tomato sauce and topped with two eggs and fontina cheese.  served with flour tortillas."  $11.)  Very reminiscent of Green Eggs Cafe's "kitchen sink," this came with everything in a ceramic dish covered in cheese and a fresh sprinkle of basil.  I actually think it beat the Kitchen Sink as far as the combination of flavors.  Tasted my friend's dish and her's was a great combination of flavors too.  Delicious and affordable.  Our bill was only a little over $20.  Fair warning: cash only and no morning drinks here!

How do you make the world's best comfort food - macaroni and cheese - even better?  Why add lobster of course!

Was in Philly for one night for business and the concierge at the Marriott got us reservations here.  Despite being a Wednesday night, the restaurant and bar were doing a brisk business and we were glad we had reservations.

There was a lot of food sharing going on at our table, so I did get to try a handful of items.  The "fresh vegetables" side dish turned out to be an incredibly delicious steamed squash dish, and as mentioned previously, the lobster mac & cheese was "to die for"!

The wine list is twice as long as the food menu, but some good selections at not quite too expensive prices.  The wait staff was fantastic and took care of my group's incredibly picky substitutions, alterations and requests with a smile.

Felt like the meal was a little pricier than it should have been, but definitely a great place if you're out for a business dinner and/or on an expense account.

We arrived very late for dinner (9:30pm) so they were out of a lot of specials like their dover sole/branzino, bone marrow, sweetbread (really wanted to try sweetbread!).

The restaurant is very intimate: seats around 30 people. BYOB makes the place very affordable. The price is extremely reasonable. For 3 course meals with sparkling water, coffee...it was about $55 per person including tax and tip. If this place were in NYC, it would easily cost double. 5 stars for value for sure.

The seared foie and scallops were excellent. The pig foot dish was a bit too mushy for me (I am used to the Korean steamed version which is a bit chewier) but still nicely flavored. Also I found the escargo to be too soft although the flavor was good.

Overall ALL the dishes were nicely flavored...especially the sauces were seasoned just right: not too salty, not too bland, just right. And the portions were just perfect amount for a 3-course-meal.

At the end of the meal, the chef came out and talked to us for a bit: a bit of extra caring touch to the meal. (I love when they do that!). I would definitely come back.

A cute coffee shop on Fairmount Ave with modern options!

Food:
The menu boasts a mix of modern diner and coffee-shop fair - from sandwiches to pancakes to pastries. While nothing blew me away, everything I've eaten here has been tasty and well portioned. There are plenty of gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options as well as some healthy/super-food choices that will please most dietary restrictions. 

Drinks:
As it should be the coffee is the star here! It's what you'd expect - with all of the options and quality you'd expect from a great coffee house. There is also a selection of seasonal smoothies which I've enjoyed. You can't go wrong here!

Service:
Service is friendly and timely.

Value:
The reason OCF gets 4 stars are the prices. While not necessarily outrageous, some of the prices and up-charges are a little hard to swallow. I could definitely see why some people would consider this place overpriced. My recommendation is to take a look at the menu and determine where you fall - if you find the prices acceptable than go for it, everything is great!

I ordered the stuffed meatball, which was very good and reasonably priced. When I received my meal I realized that the relatively low price was due to the smaller than average portion size. As a small person, It was a satisfying portion for me and I didn't leave overstuffed; However, my friend was still a little hungry at the end of the meal, although he enjoyed his steak. 
The restaurant lighting was very dim, which can be nice and romantic, but in my opinion it was slightly too dark for what I like in a restaurant.
Overall, wonderful experience, food, and service. Only downside is the portion size, but the price makes it worth it.

Even if I did not live close to this place, I would still drive at least a half hour just to come here for lunch or dinner because the atmosphere and the food are excellent.  Frankly, from the outside this place does not look inviting, and if you're not familiar with the area, it is easy to miss.  On the inside, though, the place is bright, interesting, and my favorite part is the big TV.  There are pictures of menu items to make ordering easier, and a lot of the food is right there when you're ordering, so you see exactly what you're getting.  For a while I used to always get the veggie roll because it is delicious, a little spicy, and filling, and I knew I couldn't go wrong with it.  Recently I tried the lamb kabob.  WOW!  Delicious!  It is so tender and savory.  I still cannot get over the fact that this place is so little and inexpensive, but serves such delicious food, for which I could have easily paid so much more at some fancy place.  This is what I love about this place they keep it simple, affordable, and they really know how to knock your socks off with the food.

Jared and I visited on a very hot summer morning after he raved about it for months. Immediately the server came over to bring water and ask about any drink orders; not long after that, she came by again to refill our waters and to take our food orders. I decided on the sushi and sashimi platter for one, and we settled in to wait for the meal.

Our drinks arrived first, and I was awed by the size of the milkshake--it was at least 25 oz and heavenly to drink. The sushi/sashimi platter arrived with a full explanation from the server--ahi and white tuna, salmon, yellowtail, and sake-marinated tuna (both sushi and sashimi), plus a salmon maki roll. I practically inhaled the food--the fish was really fresh and the maki was rolled well.

It ran us about fifty dollars. A bit pricey for a lunch with two people--but it's definitely affordable if you order a reasonable amount of sushi (I certainly did not stick to this advice), and the food is really well-crafted, so you are getting your money's worth. Plus the size of the milkshake. Come on, you know you want it.

Exceptional food, drinks, and service. Go here and you will be happy. I also appreciated that it's not overly formal or stuffy. 

It's expensive, yes, but I think it's actually a good value - less expensive than some lesser restaurants in the area.

low key expensive for the quality of food but it's still a good experience overall. the waitress was knowledgeable about the menu, friendly and made an effort to converse with my friends and I. the vibe was nice and the decor was eccentric. definitely a cool dining experience for dog lovers.

I was recommended this place by a Philly resident, and wow, it was delicious! Let me start be saying that I love tacos de lengua (that's tongue) and I LOVE horchata. If a restaurant does not serve horchata, best believe I will be leaving that place ASAP. This place had both! The host was very kind and brought me chips and salsas. Now, when the 3 tacos arrived, I was a bit shook by how the lengua was cut up, never had I eaten tongue like that. Usually, lengua is like diced up in small pieces, but this look like the lengua had been sliced in a machine or something--I don't know. Nevertheless, I took a bite and it was delicious. The tacos had the typical double tortilla that every taco has no matter where you go. I was only able to eat two tacos though and took the third to-go. I wasn't even able to drink all the horchata either, which was a shame because it was sooo good! Also, it was fairly affordable for what I ordered. 

Definitely check this place out!
You're definitely paying for the experience which is amazing! The food is pretty good but not worth the price you pay. Service is very good!!

I am so sad to have to write this review - I've been waiting for years to go here. My boyfriend and I decided that our one-year anniversary would the perfect time to try it. Sadly, we were incredibly disappointed in our experience. 
We had a reservation and arrived on time, but our table wasn't ready - not a big deal, but the hostess steered us directly to the bar and said "go have a drink". It sort of felt like a ploy. Once we ordered a drink and had one sip, someone came to get us for our table. 
We were seated directly next to the waiter's computer stand, so my boyfriend stared at a computer screen all night - bummer. 
And then the food. Incredibly overpriced for what we got. My boyfriend's fish was the size of a credit card, cost $32, and was completely bland. My chicken liver rigatoni was just OK. 
Mostly I'm disappointed in the price/value ratio. We are people who are fine with paying for expensive meals - if they are delicious. This place is overpriced and simply not great.

My husband and another couple had dinner here January 21,2020. Food quality was excellent.....but the valve of the food was borderline insulting.  Portions were very small, prices were very high....$14 for a very very small plate of pasta is not acceptable.  A small portion of fish for $20 is also outrageous.  A carafe, a 3/4 carafe  of house draft red wine for $44.00 is not a good valve.  The valve to price ratio here is less than satisfying.  I felt insulted by the prices...the waitress also was pushing...small plates, 3 courses....at least 8 dishes for a table of 4.  Plain and simple...great food, too expensive for what you get...definitely an expense account place.

I really wanted to like this place...I really did. Seeing all the positive reviews gave me lots of hope. Once my wife and I stepped foot into the nicely designed restaurant, things went downhill. For starters, we had reservations but were not seated until 20 minutes after the reservation. 

Next up are issues with the bar. Bartenders seemed overwhelmed and as a result were inattentive. We were hoping that the seating issue was just an anomaly but it was compounded by this as well. 

Once we were seated the server was very inattentive and the experience was very reminiscent of the very slow service we experienced in Paris, France. Fortunately the restaurants in Paris redeemed themselves with the excellent food they served time and again. 

Lastly, to make things worse, most of the platters we were served were served room temperature. It seemed as though the food was cooked and left sitting which was probably the case all things considered.

I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. The food is overpriced and overhyped. Save your time and money and visit a more experienced, more consistent restaurant like Buddakan where you pay a decent price but receive an equally pleasing experience.

This place WAS a complete dive with awesome & affordable food 12 years ago but now it's totally overpriced. It still looks the same as it did back then, the portions are huge, the food tastes good but not for the prices. My husband and I ate here yesterday and ordered chicken and oxtail entrees with 2 extra sides and no drinks. They didn't not have all the items listed on the menu and the bill was over $50! With those kind of prices you'd expect they at least  try to improve on the service and esthetics of the restaurant. I will not come back here.

really expensive for small portions. Food was good. But...but, it was not up to the standard one would expect for the price. Just not satesfying. Also, the music and ambiance was very simple and blah. The decor was nice and eclectic.

Well, was looking forward to this but, so disappointed.  Meal was over produced, meaning too much sauce, not hot, greasy and puny for the price.  Service was great.  Kids were everywhere all crying at once.  Not a place for a quiet meal for adults, and, the biggest thing TOO EXPENSIVE FOR MEAGER SERVING AND POOR QUALITY.

I just dined at KQ for the second time.  I have to say that though the food was good, the menu is very limited (and yes I like meat!).  Most importantly, I left thinking that this place is outrageously overpriced.

I enjoy fine dining and had a thousand expensive dinners around the world. This is not fine dining in an way.  Not the food.  Not the atmosphere.

There were a few things that our party of six ordered that were just total ripoffs.  I am sorry but a 12.00 order of Brussels sprouts should have more than 4 chopped up Brussels sprouts. And a 24.00 order of mushroom ravioli should be more than a small appetizer plate size.

I enjoy good food.  I am not cheap.  But I felt this place was like "Let's see how far we can go and get away with ripping off people."

I went to this restaurant the other night with a friend and it was probably the most overpriced restaurant I've been to in a really long time. It cost $15 for the spinach artichoke dip appetizer; it was mediocre at best and came out in a STYROFOAM BOWL...(are you kidding?). The rest of the food was expensive and mediocre and the drinks were also expensive and not very strong. All in all, the bill was around $100 and it was the most underwhelming $100 I've ever spent on food/drinks. The friendly staff was the only redeeming quality.

This is the spot I took my wife after I proposed 15 years ago.  We were young and having just proposed the food was not top priority.  
We decided to eat here on our 15 year anniversary- Looking forward to a great night of good food and great scenery.  we wanted to sit outside on the porch.  We got a sitter - had a nice walk from the top parking lot to the Inn.  We were seated and waited and waited for a drink order.  My wife was dressed nicely and I was as well.  We were seated among sweaty walkers and runners and babies.  Not usually a problem but just not what we were expecting.  The food was extremely expensive to be eating among the runners.
We ordered a drink, finally, and then looked over the menu - Honestly we almost left to go to our local Italian spot - we thought "good god" we are going to spend a fortune on dinner.
we decided to stay.  Food was good - not spectacular and the price was way too high.  
Great ambiance for a casual stop in but still not worth the price.

Decent food, but too expensive for a fat casual option.

I ordered one ruben, which was tasty, but for the amount I paid, I would not return; one item was $4. My co-workers got a few items each, and while we were all happy with how the food tasted, agreed that the cost was far too high. They each paid nearly $20 for lunch. While this is expected for a sit-down meal, they barely provide service. There is no one at a cash register; instead, you pay through a tablet on the wall. With these costs cut, I don't understand why this fast casual option is the price that it is.

It was okay. The food is a little overpriced for what you get and pretty average- it's stuff you can make at home for WAY more cheap and yummy than what you get here. I was excited to try it but wasn't impressed.

Awful, overpriced, bland food. 

The whole place has a weird vibe, as others have mentioned in the reviews. It is almost as if they are trying to fool their customers into thinking they are eating at a higher-end diner. They charge downtown prices in the Fishtown area, and they dress up their menu and plates so that you feel like you are getting something special. The food does not even come close to stacking up, however. People aren't so easily fooled. If you serve someone mediocre food and they feel like they are getting ripped off, they won't be back. 

I think they should either lower their prices or increase the quality of the food. If neither is done I will not be returning.

Overpriced for what it is. The food was good but it was double the price of what it should be. Our experience was ruined by the fact that we had to wait two hours to be seated at a table despite having a reservation. I would not recommend for a large party but would go back for small plates upstairs.

This place is overpriced and overrated, even with food satefy issues.
We had 4 people, and per yelp review, we ordered the cheese plate, and for main course we had shrimp and scallop, roasted duck breast, pork belly, and steak. Here is why it is totally not worth the hype:
- The complementary appetizer (though not the main subject matter here) tastes like normal croissant we can get in a bakery, very unimpressive for such an upscale restaurant
- Most importantly: 2 of us got STOMACH UPSET after the dinner. At first I thought it was just me or something to do with my own main course, but the next day my friend told me she had the same issue. She felt really sick and even threw up after going home.
- The portion is small, combined with the food quality, would make this way overpriced ($34 pre-tax for a main course). I live in Philly for 2 years, and pretty sure that there are plenty of other restaurants with either better quality or value for money.

Anyone who thinks the food here is worth the price is smoking crack.  First time dining here will be the last.  The waitress recommended 3-4 orders per person.  We had a party of 3 and ordered 7 total dishes (so less than what she recommended).  This cost us $39 per person (including tax and tip).  $39!

Now, I'm not against high prices if it's spent wisely (Alma de Cuba, Amada, Le Bec Fin, to name a few).  But the portions for these small plates are unacceptably tiny.  

Small portions, high prices--fine, I'll deal with it if the food is awesome.  It wasn't.  Just FYI, we had the lobster roll, crab tacos, Peking duck, Korean short ribs, Korean rice cake, and Ma Po tofu, and "Philly Cheesesteak".  The only thing that was actually good was the Philly Cheesesteak, crab tacos, and Korean short ribs.  Sadly, the dishes were NOT so good as to justify the ridiculous price.  

Recommendation: take a pass on this restaurant.  Not that great and way too expensive.  Our end of dinner conversation was spent discussing where else we could have spent 40 bucks.  

Oh, did I mention the small portions and ludicrous prices?

You know those aspects of your life that you keep around because they're JUST good enough? Maybe it's that streaming service that you pay for every month with the annoying buffering and obscene amount of commercials, just because it's the only place that has your favorite series. Maybe it's that POS car that you're been driving for ten years that is more reliable than your mom's anxious phone calls, but is one mechanical problem away from being sold for scraps. Or maybe it's that significant other who you've been drifting apart from, who is starting to annoy the crap out of you, and is one smart-ass comment away from ending up in the pile of lovers past. 

Well, Valley Green Inn is the complete embodiment of all of those things in your life that you like just BARELY enough not to kick it to the curb. It is just charming enough that you'll overlook the $18 fried cauliflower, absurdly priced glasses of wine, and the too-good-for-you atmosphere. The food is overpriced and underwhelming, and the only reason that they can charge what they do is because they have no competition. 

I have frequented this establishment for years, willing to overlook this fact, just because it's convenient and charming. Today, I had horrible service, and that was all that I needed to kick this restaurant off of my "good enough" list for good. Never. Going. Back.
Food was overpriced but very, very good.  The problem?:  you expect superior service in this price range.  Service was inferior.

Over priced. Over stuffy. Not worth it. It's the typical Chestnut Hill restaurant with the typical attitude. Serve mediocre food at high prices, but get away with it bc it's Chestnut Hill. Plain and simple.

      "expected_direction": "positive或negative",
      "evidence_span": "从对应review_text逐字复制的连续原文"
    }
  ]
}

drafts必须恰好有4项，且必须是2项positive和2项negative。
